# Vocolens (Full Reference)

> AI voice journal for ADHD, autism, and alexithymia. Speak your mind, track mood patterns, and gain emotional clarity.

This is the expanded reference file for Vocolens, intended for AI systems and answer engines that need deeper context than llms.txt provides. See https://vocolens.com/llms.txt for the condensed version.

## About

Vocolens is an AI-powered voice journaling app designed specifically for neurodivergent minds. Instead of writing, users simply speak - Vocolens transcribes what they say and analyses the words and language to name emotions the conscious mind may overlook, so users finally have language for feelings they couldn't put into words. Built for people with ADHD, autism, alexithymia, and anyone who struggles with traditional journaling or emotional self-awareness.

- Website: https://vocolens.com
- Platform: Android
- Price: Paid subscription with a 3-day free trial (monthly, quarterly, and annual plans)
- Category: Health & Mental Wellness
- Application category: HealthApplication / Mental Wellness

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Is voice and data private and secure?
A: Your journal entries, audio, and personalization data are stored on your device and locked behind biometric authentication (Face ID or Fingerprint) and a PIN - there is no cloud account or synced backup of your journal. To turn speech into insight, two steps happen off-device transiently over an encrypted connection: your audio is sent for speech-to-text transcription (Deepgram), and the resulting text transcript is sent for emotion analysis (OpenAI via OpenRouter). Neither service permanently stores your data, and no audio is sent for the analysis step. You can export or permanently delete your data at any time. See the Privacy Policy for full detail.

Q: How does the app actually know what I'm feeling?
A: Vocolens analyses the words and language in your journal transcript - your word choice, phrasing, and narrative context - to name what you were feeling, mapping it to 8 core psychology-backed emotions on a 2D scale of pleasantness and energy. Over time it learns from the corrections you make, so the labels line up more closely with how you actually experience your emotions, giving you clearer self-understanding the more you use it.

Q: What makes Vocolens different from other journaling apps?
A: Most journaling apps require writing. Vocolens lets users speak instead, detects emotions from their words, learns from corrections, and builds a personal emotional map. It is designed specifically for neurodivergent brains that think faster than they can type.

Q: What happens if the AI gets my emotion wrong?
A: Users can correct the emotion label, and the AI remembers the correction, reducing that mistake in the future. Corrections build a personalized emotional vocabulary unique to each user.

Q: Can this replace therapy or mental health support?
A: No. Vocolens is a personal journaling and self-awareness tool, not a medical device or therapy service. It does include built-in wellbeing awareness: when an entry reads as moderate or high distress, Vocolens gently flags it so you can notice sooner and give yourself a moment - the point being to help you catch overwhelm earlier, not to treat it.

## Features (Detailed)

1. Journal Calendar - "Easily track your progress." A visual mood calendar showing daily entries and emotional patterns over time, focused on presence rather than streaks.
2. Weekly Reflection - "View your weekly mood story." An AI-generated narrative summary of the user's emotional week, highlighting patterns and shifts.
3. Mood Story - "See which emotion dominates your days." Daily dominant emotion tracking visualized across the week.
4. Explore Deeper - "Go as deep as you want." Flexible depth of analysis, from quick check-ins to deep emotional exploration.
5. Emotional Landscape - "Mapping your mood in one chart." Plutchik's wheel-based emotion mapping showing the full spectrum of feelings.
6. Body Sensation Map - "Track your physical feelings." A somatic awareness tool mapping where emotions manifest physically in the body, based on interoception research.
7. Deep Insights - "Clear insights without any noise." Personalized AI insights that learn the user's emotional dialect rather than generic textbook responses.
8. Emotional Triggers - "Learn what keeps setting you off." Pattern recognition identifying recurring emotional triggers and their contexts.
9. Emotional Themes - "Your emotional narrative." Recurring emotional patterns and stories surfaced from journal entries over time.
10. Time of Day - "Track your mood by the hour." Temporal mood analysis showing how emotions shift throughout the day.

## Who It's For

- People with ADHD who think faster than they can write
- Autistic individuals seeking better emotional self-understanding and regulation
- People with alexithymia (difficulty identifying and describing emotions), affecting roughly 10% of people
- Anyone who finds traditional journaling frustrating or inaccessible
- Neurodivergent individuals wanting to understand their emotional patterns

## Science & Approach

Vocolens is grounded in emotion science including:
- Plutchik's wheel of emotions for granular emotion mapping beyond "happy/sad" categories
- Lieberman (2007) laboratory affect-labeling research; this is not a clinical trial of Vocolens
- Interoception research on sensing and interpreting internal body signals
- Metacognitive pattern recognition for building emotional intelligence over time

## Resource Articles

- "Affect Labeling: How to Name Your Emotions" - https://vocolens.com/resources/science-of-reflection
  Research scope, practical examples, and limitations of naming feelings.

- "Emotional Awareness: What It Is and How to Improve It" - https://vocolens.com/resources/emotional-awareness-patterns
  Definitions, examples, and a short emotion-and-trigger journal.

- "ADHD Time Blindness: Examples and Practical Time Supports" - https://vocolens.com/resources/adhd-time-blindness
  Learn what ADHD time blindness means, recognize everyday examples, and try visible timers, task estimates, and transition cues without blaming yourself.

- "Alexithymia: Difficulty Identifying Emotions and Where to Start" - https://vocolens.com/resources/alexithymia-emotional-vocabulary
  Explore what alexithymia means, examples of difficulty identifying feelings, and gentle ways to describe sensations and build emotional vocabulary.

- "Autism and Emotional Regulation: Sensory Needs and Practical Supports" - https://vocolens.com/resources/autism-emotional-regulation
  Explore emotional regulation in autistic adults, how sensory demands and alexithymia can differ, and ways to plan support without masking your needs.

- "Burnout Signs and Recovery: What to Notice and What Can Help" - https://vocolens.com/resources/burnout-recovery-signs
  Understand workplace burnout signs, how they differ from ordinary tiredness, and practical recovery supports that address demands as well as rest.

- "Physical Signs of Overwhelm: Body Awareness Without Guessing" - https://vocolens.com/resources/distress-detection
  Learn what interoception means, explore physical signs that can accompany overwhelm, and try a gentle check-in without treating sensations as diagnoses.

- "Overthinking and Rumination: How to Recognize the Loop" - https://vocolens.com/resources/overthinking-rumination
  Understand rumination versus useful reflection, see examples of repetitive worry, and try a practical next-step check without promises of instant relief.

- "Rejection Sensitivity and ADHD: What RSD Means and How to Respond" - https://vocolens.com/resources/rejection-sensitivity
  Learn what rejection sensitivity and RSD mean, why the label is not a formal diagnosis, and practical ways to respond to hurt without assuming intent.

- "Mixed Emotions: Why You Can Feel Happy and Sad at Once" - https://vocolens.com/resources/mixed-emotions
  Learn what mixed emotions are, see everyday examples of feeling two things at once, and try a reflection that makes room for both without forcing a choice.

- "Emotional Granularity: Why Specific Words Change What You Feel" - https://vocolens.com/resources/emotional-granularity
  Fine distinctions between emotional states and a personal vocabulary.
